info.name: Event Ticketing & Management System - Backend API
info.description:
Full backend API collection generated from the Node.js/Express + MongoDB backend (auth, events, categories, cart, wishlist, ticket tiers, tickets, payments/Razorpay, blog, newsletter, contact, analytics).

## Setup
1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable (default `http://localhost:3009`).
2. Run **Auth > Register User**, verify the email (check console/log for the link if email isn't configured), then run **Auth > Login** — this auto-saves `accessToken`/`refreshToken`/`userId` as collection variables used by every other request.
3. For admin-only routes, log in with a user whose `role` is `admin` (see `seedAdmin.js` in the backend, or promote a user directly in MongoDB).
4. Typical happy-path flow: Category > Create Category → Event > Create Event → Ticket Tier > Create Ticket Tier → Ticket > Purchase Ticket → Payment > Create Razorpay Order → (complete checkout on the client / Razorpay test mode) → Payment > Verify Payment.

All protected routes use collection-level Bearer auth (`{{accessToken}}`); public routes override this with 'No Auth'.

## Payment routes were failing for the whole team — root cause & fix
The issue wasn't in the payment code itself. `app/config/passport.js` unconditionally constructed a Google OAuth `Strategy`, and `passport-google-oauth20` throws synchronously at require time if `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`/`GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` aren't set. Since nobody had Google OAuth wired up locally (and no route even uses it — `googleLogin` in authController is orphaned), the **entire server crashed on boot** for anyone without those three env vars, taking every route down with it, payments included. Fixed by only registering the Google strategy when those env vars are actually present. Verified by restarting the server and exercising Payment > Create Razorpay Order and Payment > Verify Payment end-to-end against Razorpay test-mode keys — both now return 200/201 as expected.

Separately (not code bugs, but will also block testing if unset in your local `.env`): `RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is read by `verifyWebhookSignature` but was missing from `.env.example` — added. And this repo's own `.env` had a `CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET` that doesn't match its `CLOUDINARY_API_KEY`/`CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME` (confirmed via a direct `cloudinary.api.ping()` call, which returned `api_secret mismatch`) — that blocks event-banner and ticket-QR uploads specifically, not the payment routes themselves; get a fresh secret from the Cloudinary dashboard if you hit upload errors.

item.name: Auth

request.description: Creates a new user account (role defaults to 'user'). Sends a verification email; the account cannot log in until verified.
Verifies the email address using the token & user id sent in the verification email link.
Authenticates a verified user. Sets accessToken/refreshToken/userId collection variables automatically from the response.
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access/refresh token pair. Works via cookie or via refreshToken in the body.
Requests a password reset email.
Resets the account password using the token & user id from the password reset email link.
Changes the logged-in user's password. Requires auth.
Invalidates the refresh token and clears auth cookies. Requires auth.
Returns the authenticated user's profile.

Public. Not a normal API call — open this URL in a browser tab (not via Postman's Send button) to kick off the Google OAuth consent flow. Redirects to Google, then Google redirects back to 'Google OAuth Callback' below. Only registered if GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET/GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL are set on the server; otherwise returns 503.

Public. Never call this directly — Google's own redirect after 'Google Login' hits this URL with a real authorization code. On success it sets accessToken/refreshToken cookies and redirects to FRONTEND_URL. Must match the exact 'Authorized redirect URI' configured on the Google Cloud OAuth client, or Google returns redirect_uri_mismatch. Included here for documentation only.
